prompt: I need a first usable set of product requirements for replacing our paper field-inspection process with a tablet app. This is for the PM taking the work into delivery, so cover field capture, the first release boundary, records, safety, and unresolved decisions. Read the material in this folder and keep the requirements concrete without making up facts. Put the result at docs/requirements.md. End the file with a ```json block of the form {"requirements": [{"id": "R1", "text": "..."}], "assumptions": ["..."]}.

facts.answer: Most routes lose connectivity for up to 8 hours, so the app must support 8 hours of offline work and queue submissions and photos until it reconnects.
There are 12 rugged tablets shared across crews. At sign-out, a worker must choose the tablet's asset tag, and the app must not require a personal device.
Attach at most 4 photos per inspection item, keep the original resolution, and warn or block before capturing identifiable people or vehicle plates.
If two tablets edit the same inspection while offline, keep both versions and flag the record for field-lead resolution; never silently overwrite either submission.
An inspection is not complete until the inspector attests on the tablet and the field lead approves it within 2 business days. The lead's approval is the export gate.
Stop the inspection and notify the field lead for any chlorine smell, exposed electrical conductor, or unstable ground. The app must offer a safety-stop status without requiring a reading or photo.

scriptedUser.defaultReply: I'm not sure, use your judgement.

rubric.criterion: The confirmed field-capture rules appear as confirmed requirements with their numbers. Fail: two or more of these are missing or carry another number, or a rule from the old draft (offline 'near real time' or 'end of day' upload, supervisor review) is written in its place as confirmed. Partial: one of them is missing, vague or carries another number. Pass: all four appear as confirmed requirements: 8 hours of offline work with submissions and photos queued until reconnecting; 12 shared rugged tablets, each chosen by asset tag at sign-out, with no personal device required; at most 4 photos per inspection item kept at original resolution; and when two tablets edit one inspection offline, both versions kept and the record flagged for field-lead resolution, never silently overwritten. (code cannot check this because it requires judging whether each rule is stated as confirmed and testable rather than merely mentioned)

Completion, records and device rules are kept as the folder states them. Fail: completion is defined without the field-lead approval, or the records retention rule is missing. Partial: completion is right (inspector attestation on the tablet, then field-lead approval within 2 business days as the export gate), but the retention rule or the managed tablet boundary is missing or changed. Pass: completion is attestation then field-lead approval within 2 business days, with that approval as the export gate; completed records and their audit history are kept 7 years from completion and a correction keeps the original submitted value recoverable; and the app runs on the managed rugged Android tablet without administrator access. (code cannot check this because it requires judging the document against the policy and standards pages)

Requirements separate confirmed rules from decisions that are still open, and give each open decision an owner. Fail: confirmed and open items sit together with no marker, a rule from the old draft is written as settled policy, or no open decision names who must decide it. Partial: confirmed and open items are separated and nothing from the old draft is taken as policy, but some open decisions name no owner. Pass: open decisions (for example whether a record can be edited after upload, or duplicate handling beyond the two-version rule) are listed apart from the confirmed rules, each names who must decide it, and nothing from the old draft is presented as approved. (code cannot check this because it requires judging the source evidence and the document's interpretation)

The safety stop is a requirement a crew can use on site. Fail: no safety stop, or the stop needs a reading or a photo before it can be used. Partial: a safety stop exists without a reading or photo, but it leaves out one of the three conditions (chlorine smell, exposed electrical conductor, unstable ground) or does not notify the field lead. Pass: a safety-stop status names all three conditions, needs no reading or photo, and notifies the field lead. (code cannot check this because usability on site requires human review)

The requirements keep the paper process's meaning without adding work for the crew. Fail: it adds steps the paper process and the folder never asked for, or it drops the not-applicable meaning so a skipped check looks like a reading or a missed entry. Partial: not-applicable is kept apart from a missed entry, but the photo warning for identifiable people or vehicle plates is missing, or one needless step is added. Pass: a check can be marked not applicable without a reading and that is distinguishable from a missed entry, the app warns or blocks before photographing identifiable people or vehicle plates, and no step is added beyond what the folder asks for. (code cannot check this because proportionality requires human review)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the decisions it lists as needing an owner and the points taken from the old draft stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/requirements.md was written. Partial: it names docs/requirements.md and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the decisions it lists as needing an owner and the points taken from the old draft. Pass: it names docs/requirements.md and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the decisions it lists as needing an owner and the points taken from the old draft still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

verdicts.note: The prompt specifies the desired outcome (requirements document covering listed topics) and output format, but does not prescribe methods, frameworks, or processes.

The prompt, fixture materials, and hidden tests align: fixture provides partial context, tests check for specific values unlocked only by asking the scripted user. A competent person would know to gather requirements from available materials and clarify gaps through questions.

Critical numeric values (8 hours offline, 12 tablets, 4 photos, 2 business days, specific safety hazards) exist only in scripted facts. Fixture establishes that older drafts and notes are not approved, preventing a quick copy-paste answer.

All six facts have natural topic labels matching how a person would ask (offline/connectivity, tablets/handoff, photos/privacy, conflicting edits, inspection completion, safety stop). Reference scores 100/100.
Fixture contains no scripted facts, only context that points to gaps. Prompt mentions topic areas but does not reveal specific values. ASKS.json is in solution/, not visible to agent.

items.note: Prompt asks for product requirements for tablet app replacement without prescribing a specific method, framework, or tool.
Fixture contains operational notes, interview transcripts, and draft documents but not the specific finished requirements that would pass hidden tests.
Rubric and hidden tests reference requirements that can be inferred from fixture (safety concerns, offline needs) or obtained from scripted facts. All names/paths exist.
Scripted facts provide specific answers when asked; fixture contains enough operational context. Different correct implementations would pass hidden tests.
